speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Ministry will consider implementing recommendations from the "Stay-at-home Fathers" study conducted by an Institute of Policy Studies researcher, especially the recommendation that exclusive, non-transferable paternity leave should be increased.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Greater paternal involvement in the home also helps mothers to stay active in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Local research has shown that Singaporean fathers are playing a more active role in caregiving and family responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have progressively increased parental leave for fathers over the years to better support working parents and help fathers to play an active role in caring for their children.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This took into account feedback from some parents that shared parental leave was helpful in allowing fathers and mothers to decide flexibly how best to care for their child, based on their own family circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We are also mindful of the need to carefully balance the needs of parents with the concerns of employers over the needs at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The study by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) recognised that fathers' roles are also shaped by societal norms.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) partners non-profit organisations, such as the Centre for Fathering, to promote the "Dads for Life" and "Mums for Life" movements in schools, workplaces and the wider community.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These movements go a long way in driving mindset shifts among employers, colleagues, friends and families, to give greater recognition and support to the important roles fathers and mothers play in the lives of their children.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government will continue to work with business and community partners to promote greater paternal involvement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I just get the Ministry's response to the IPS study which said that our policies actually continue to signal that childcare is a woman's responsibility and that they reinforce this gender stereotype.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, whether we are going to review the Shared Parental Leave policy as well, which was one of the IPS recommendations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, the IPS' was a very small scale study.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am wondering whether the Prime Minister's Office or MSF can do a larger scale study to really look into this issue?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are entitled to putting forward a point of view.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not necessarily agree or disagree with them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we can look specifically at their proposals and, in that regard, the policies are never static.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are continuously being reviewed and continuously being enhanced where there are opportunities to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But at different junctures, we would have to look at what is of greater priority.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And for these, the Government itself conducts surveys; the Government itself engages with different groups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And that is what we have put a lot of emphasis on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to what could change in the future, can we perhaps even strengthen it more, that would be a relevant question for further review.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
